# 2025 World Seniors Championship

The **2025 World Seniors Championship** (officially the **2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Championship**) was a seniors snooker tournament held at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, England, from 7 to 11 May 2025. It was the 15th edition of the World Seniors Championship, first held in 1991. Organised by World Seniors Snooker, the event featured 16 players aged 40 or over, competing in a single-elimination format. English player Alfie Burden won the tournament, defeating Jersey's Aaron Canavan 8–4 in the final to claim his first World Seniors title. Burden earned £20,000 in prize money for the victory. The tournament was broadcast in the United Kingdom on Channel 5 and 5 Action.

The defending champion was Brazil's Igor Figueiredo, who had won the 2024 event by defeating Ken Doherty in the final. Figueiredo was eliminated in the first round in 2025. The event marked the debuts of several former professional players on the seniors circuit, including Joe Perry and Dominic Dale, who had recently fallen off the main World Snooker Tour. Jimmy White, a four-time champion and the most successful player in the tournament's history, reached the first round but was defeated.

## Format

The 2025 tournament introduced a revised format following an announcement by World Seniors Snooker in March 2025. The first round and quarter-finals were played as the best of seven frames, the semi-finals as the best of 11 frames, and the final as the best of 15 frames. This change aimed to provide more competitive matches while maintaining accessibility for senior players.

Players qualified through various routes, including invitations based on past achievements, World Seniors Tour rankings, and regional qualifiers. The minimum age for participation was 40 for amateurs and 45 for players from the professional tour ranked outside the top 64. One spot was determined via a "Golden Ticket" play-off held in April 2025, which was won by Alfie Burden after defeating Matthew Ford 4–3 in the final.

## Participants

The field consisted of 16 players:

- Igor Figueiredo (Brazil, defending champion)
- Jimmy White (England, four-time champion)
- Ken Doherty (Republic of Ireland, 1997 World Champion and two-time World Seniors runner-up)
- Aaron Canavan (Jersey, 2018 World Seniors champion)
- Tony Drago (Malta)
- Joe Perry (England)
- Dominic Dale (Wales)
- Tony Knowles (England)
- Gerard Greene (Northern Ireland)
- Alfie Burden (England)
- Craig Steadman (England)
- Andrew Norman (England)
- Wayne Townsend (England)
- Hassan Kerde (Syria)
- Charl Jonck (South Africa)
- Fabio Anderson Luersen (Brazil, Pan American qualifier)

The participants included a mix of former World Snooker Tour professionals and regional champions, with Figueiredo as the top seed.

## Tournament summary

The tournament began on 7 May with the first round. Defending champion Igor Figueiredo was eliminated early, losing 2–4 to Wayne Townsend. Jimmy White, seeking a record fifth title, fell 1–4 to Alfie Burden in a rematch of the 2023 final. Other notable first-round results included Dominic Dale's 4–2 win over Craig Steadman and Joe Perry's 4–2 victory against Fabio Anderson Luersen.

In the quarter-finals on 9 May, Aaron Canavan advanced with a 4–2 win over Townsend, while Dale defeated Perry 4–1. Burden edged out Tony Drago 4–3, and Hassan Kerde beat Charl Jonck 4–2.

The semi-finals took place on 10 May. Canavan overcame Dale 6–5 in a close contest, while Burden dominated Kerde 6–2 to reach his second World Seniors final.

### Final

The final was held on 11 May between Alfie Burden and Aaron Canavan. Burden took an early lead, winning the first session 5–3. He extended his advantage in the evening session, securing the title with an 8–4 victory. Key moments included Burden's breaks of 74, 87, and 78 in the opening frames. Canavan mounted a brief comeback by winning three consecutive frames to trail 5–4, but Burden responded with three straight frames to clinch the match.

Burden described the win as a career highlight, noting the significance of triumphing at the Crucible Theatre. Canavan, appearing in his first World Seniors final, praised Burden's performance and expressed satisfaction with his own run.

## Main draw

## Prize money

The breakdown of prize money for the tournament was as follows:

- Winner: £20,000
- Runner-up: £10,000
- Semi-finalists: £5,000 each
- Quarter-finalists: £2,500 each
- First-round losers: £1,000 each

The total prize fund remained unchanged from the 2024 event.

## Century breaks

There were no century breaks recorded during the tournament.

The 2025 World Seniors Championship showcased competitive snooker among veteran players, with Burden's victory highlighting the event's appeal to those no longer on the main professional tour. The format adjustments were well-received, providing longer matches in later stages without extending the overall schedule. Broadcast coverage on Channel 5 increased visibility, drawing attention to seniors snooker as a viable platform for former professionals. Participants like Perry and Dale, who had recently retired from the main tour, added fresh interest, potentially attracting more high-profile entries in future editions. The event continued the Crucible's tradition as the home of world championship snooker, with a contract in place to host until at least 2027.

Qualification processes emphasized global representation, with spots allocated to winners of continental championships such as the Pan American and All-Africa events. For instance, Fabio Anderson Luersen qualified via the 2024 Pan American Seniors Championship, while Charl Jonck represented Africa. The "Golden Ticket" qualifier allowed additional access, won by Burden in a separate event held in April 2025 at the Crucible Club.

The tournament's history traces back to 1991, when it was first staged as a one-off event won by Cliff Wilson. It was relaunched in 2010 with increased prize money and has been held annually since, except for 2014. Jimmy White holds the record with four titles (2010, 2019, 2020, 2023), followed by players like Peter Lines (2016) and Aaron Canavan (2018). The 2025 edition maintained the event's focus on players aged 40 and over, balancing experience with competitive integrity.

Broadcast and sponsorship played key roles, with JenningsBet as the title sponsor and Channel 5 providing live coverage in the UK. Afternoon sessions aired on Channel 5, while evenings were on 5 Action. This exposure helped promote the World Seniors Tour, which includes additional events throughout the year.

Referees included international officials, with Bulgaria's Proletina Velichkova officiating part of the final. The event ran smoothly, with no reported controversies, and received positive feedback from players and spectators. Burden's post-match comments emphasized enjoying the moment at the iconic venue, reflecting the tournament's blend of nostalgia and competition.

=========================================================================================================

 Mark Mothershaw  Updated: 10 Nov 25 15:12 

**The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship takes place between Wednesday 7th and Sunday 11th May and we've got all the details you need to know ahead of the Sheffield-staged spectacular**

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Dates
---------------------------------------------

### When is the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship gets underway on Wednesday 7th May, two days after the conclusion of the 2025 World Snooker Championship, and runs through until Sunday 11th May.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Venue
---------------------------------------------

### Where is the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship taking place?

The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will be held at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield, with the fabled venue now synonymous with the event.

Previously being staged in cities such as Stoke-on-Trent, Peterborough and Blackpool, Sheffield has been the competition's home since 2019, meaning the 2025 staging will be the seventh successive year that it will have been held there.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Age Limit
-------------------------------------------------

### What is the age limit to play at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The minimum age for players on the main tour but outside the top 64 was reverted to 45 years ahead of the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship, whilst the minimum age for amateur players remained at 40.

In the past the minimum age limit has varied between both 40 and 45.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Players
-----------------------------------------------

### Who is playing at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship?

Sixteen players have been confirmed to feature at the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship, including defending champion Igor Figueiredo.

Four-time event winner Jimmy White is also amongst the field as are former ranking event champions Ken Doherty, Dominic Dale and Joe Perry, both of whom officially retired from the professional stage earlier this year.

2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship Previous Winners
--------------------------------------------------------

A total of 12 players have been crowned World Seniors Snooker Champion since the inaugural staging of the event in 1991, including 2024 champion Igor Figueiredo.

### Who has the most World Seniors Snooker Championship wins?

Jimmy White is the most decorated player in World Seniors Snooker Championship history, winning the prestigious tournament on four occasions.

In total, 'The Whirlwind', who famously lost all seven of his World Snooker Championship finals, has reached the final on six occasions, losing just two of them.

His most recent triumph came in 2023 when he saw off Alfie Burden in the showpiece, having previously reigned supreme in 2020, 2019 and 2010.

History of the World Seniors Snooker Championship
-------------------------------------------------

### When was the first World Seniors Snooker Championship?

The World Seniors Snooker Championship was launched back in 1991 when Welshman Cliff Wilson edged past Australian Eddie Charlton in dramatic fashion in Stoke-on-Trent.

That was the one and only occasion it took place prior to 2010 however, when the World Seniors Tour was re-branded and relaunched, with greater prize money, helping to attract higher profile players including Jimmy White.

Since 2010, the event has been staged every year, with the exception of 2014.

### How does the World Seniors Snooker Championship work?

A single game of snooker is known as a frame, with the winner being decided by which player has scored the most points by the time all the balls have been potted on the table or if there are not enough points available for the player that is trailing to be able to mount a comeback.

Most snooker matches at professional level are contested over more than just a one-frame format.

For example the first round of the World Seniors Snooker Championship will be played over a best-of-seven frame format, essentially meaning the first player to four frames is the winner.

Matches in the quarter-finals remain over the same length, before they expand to best-of-11 in the semi-finals and then best-of-15 in the showpiece final.

### How many frames are played in World Seniors Snooker Championship games?

First-round matches are the best-of-seven frames contests, the same length as the four quarter-final ties. Semi-finals then expand to a best-of-11 format before the final is played out over 15 frames.

*   Final - Best-of-15 frames
*   Semi-Finals - Best-of-11 frames
*   Quarter-Finals - Best-of-seven frames
*   Last 16 - Best-of-seven frames

### How much will the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship winner get?

The prize money for the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will remain unchanged from 2024 with the winner set to receive £20,000 and the runner-up taking home a cool £10,000.

Format Change Announced for 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship
===================================================================

19th March 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Format Change Announced for 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship

**World Seniors Snooker (WSS) is pleased to announce a change to the format of the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship which will take place at the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield on 7-11 May.**

All rounds up to and including the quarter-finals will now be the best-of-seven frames, while the semi-finals will now best best-of-11 frames and the final will be contested over the best-of-15 frames.

![Image 5: Snooker player is waving as he is entering on stage with the cue in his hand](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/White2-300x200.jpg)

Brazil’s Igor Figueiredo made history for South America by winning the flagship title last May and he will open proceedings on the opening Wednesday afternoon. Jimmy ‘The Whirlwind’ White, a record four-time champion, and two-time runner-up Ken Doherty are both set to begin their campaigns on the afternoon of Thursday 8 May.

[**Tickets remain available for the World Seniors Championship and start from just £17.50.**](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025)

**The 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship will take place this week with the likes of Igor Figueiredo and Jimmy White in the draw.**

The prestigious event on the World Seniors Snooker Tour will return to the Crucible Theatre in Sheffield for the seventh year in a row from May 7th to 11th.

There will be 16 players in the field this year, with Brazil’s Figueiredo representing the top seed as the [reigning champion](https://snookerhq.com/2024/05/12/igor-figueiredo-wins-world-seniors-snooker-championship/) and record four-time winner White on the opposite side of the draw.

Who is in the 2025 World Seniors Championship draw?
---------------------------------------------------

Joining Figeuredo and White will be a high-quality group of players in what is a very competitive lineup for an edition of the World Seniors Snooker Championship.

Figueiredo will launch his defence against Wayne Townsend, with White first in action against Alfie Burden in a repeat of the 2023 final.

It was recently announced that the Whirlwind would receive a [fresh two-year invitational card](https://snookerhq.com/2025/04/25/jimmy-white-receives-world-snooker-tour-lifeline/) to compete on the professional World Snooker Tour.

But the seniors circuit is where he has enjoyed the most success over the last decade or so, capturing a record eight titles and appearing in several other title-deciding encounters.

Elsewhere, two-time former world seniors runner-up Ken Doherty will face South African qualifier Charl Jonck with 2018 champion Aaron Canavan up against Andrew Norman.

Joining the World Seniors Tour in 2025 will be Joe Perry and Dominic Dale, meanwhile.

Both Perry and Dale confirmed their respective retirements from professional snooker in April after more than three decades on the main tour.

But neither has plans to give up the game entirely, and they will both represent serious threats to land the silverware in Sheffield.

Perry’s first outing of the competition will be against Fabio Anderson Luersen with Dale playing Craig Steadman, and the pair of former ranking event winners could clash as early as the quarter-finals.

One of the ties of the opening round sees Tony Drago – a semi-finalist in 2024 – meet Gerard Greene.

Tony Knowles is also back for another crack with the former world number two in action against Australian Hassan Kerde in the last 16.

Who are the betting favourites?
-------------------------------

Ken Doherty, a finalist last year and also the runner-up in 2020 when he blew a 4-0 lead in the final, is considered the outright betting favourite.

The Irishman has odds of 11/4 to go all the way to glory in the World Seniors Snooker Championship draw for the first time.

Joe Perry is next at 7/2 with Igor Figueiredo considered a 5/1 chance of securing successive successes in Sheffield.

The bookies have Jimmy White at only 6/1 in the outright betting market with [askgamblers.com](https://www.askgamblers.com/sports-betting/bonuses/free-bets) providing a list of popular sportbooks that have sign-up offers and free bets to avail of.

What is the format?
-------------------

It was announced that there will be an increase to the format this year, with longer matches adding to the drama that is bound to unfold.

The first two rounds will now be played over seven frames with 11 frames subsequently required for each semi-final.

The final on May 11th will then take place over 15 frames, marking a considerable increase from the previous best-of-nine finales.

How to watch the tournament?
----------------------------

Viewers in the United Kingdom and in some parts of Ireland will be able to watch the 2025 World Seniors Snooker Championship live on Channel 5.

Tickets are [still available](https://www.sheffieldtheatres.co.uk/events/world-seniors-snooker-championship-2025) for some sessions if you want to see the action in Sheffield up close and personal.

It was recently announced that the Crucible Theatre will continue to host the World Seniors Snooker Championship until at least 2027.

What happened last year?
------------------------

In 2024, an emotional Igor Figueiredo won one of the biggest titles of his career with a [5-2 victory over Ken Doherty](https://snookerhq.com/2024/05/12/igor-figueiredo-wins-world-seniors-snooker-championship/) in the final.

The affable Brazilian, who enjoyed several stints as a professional player on the World Snooker Tour, beat Tessa Davidson in round one before conjuring a standout victory over reigning champion Jimmy White in the quarter-finals.

A 4-1 success over Tony Drago in the penultimate round helped him through to the final showdown, where he duly overcame favourite Doherty.

The glory earned Figueiredo a £20,000 payday and also saw him receive a lucrative invitation to the prestigious Champion of Champions in Bolton.

Alfie Burden Wins 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship
=====================================================================

12th May 2025

[Home](https://seniorssnooker.com/) » Alfie Burden Wins 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker Championship

**Alfie Burden is the 2025 JenningsBet World Seniors Snooker champion after he defeated Aaron Canavan 8-4 at the Crucible Theatre on Sunday.**

*   [Results](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/jennings-bet-world-seniors-championship-2025/results)

The 48-year-old, who was the last player to qualify for the event via the Golden Ticket Play-Off last month, came through a strong field at the famous venue to lift the most prestigious title in seniors snooker for the first time.

![Image 10: Man standing in front of a crowd, holding up a trophy in celebration](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_2336-300x200.jpg)

Burden’s campaign began with a repeat of the 2023 World Seniors Snooker Championship final and he exacted revenge on four-time winner Jimmy White, before showing his fighting qualities from 3-0 down against Maltese legend Tony Drago to advance to the semi-finals.

A comfortable 6-2 victory over Australian debutant Hassan Kerde then set up a title match meeting with 2018 champion Aaron Canavan from Jersey after he stunned Dominic Dale in the last four.

![Image 11: Two men dressed in formal black attire stand on either side of a woman holding a trophy, positioned behind a snooker table with balls on it, and a crowd is visible in the background](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0003-300x200.jpg)

The best-of-15 frame final was split into three mini-sessions of five frames and the first of these saw a moment of history as Michaela Tabb, who became the first female referee to take charge of a World Snooker Championship final in 2009, took charge of her final frames at the Crucible Theatre.

It was Canavan who broke the deadlock but the Englishman quickly hit back to take four successive frames, with help from contributions of 74 and 54, to lead 4-1 at the first interval.

![Image 12: Snooker player aiming his shot on the pool table, while the referee oversees his play](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0086-300x200.jpg)

A 75 saw the cueist from Jersey reduce the deficit before Burden once again showed off his scoring prowess by hit consecutive breaks 65, 109 and 80 to move one away from victory at 7-2.

Canavan was able to avoid defeat before the second interval as he took frame 10 and further threatened a comeback by taking the next to put the scoreline at 7-4.

![Image 13: Snooker player is lining up a shot on a green snooker table with various colored balls](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0029-300x200.jpg)

Burden admitted afterwards that, even at 7-3 ahead, he had told his coach Patsy Fagan that he “wasn’t fancying winning” but there were few signs of nerves in the title-winning frame as he fired in a flamboyant break of 76 to get over the line as an 8-4 victor.

![Image 14: A snooker player stands with a trophy between a woman and a man in a green room, with snooker balls on the table in the foreground and an audience in the background](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/D52_2318-300x200.jpg)

Following the victory, Burden said: “I’m absolutely delighted. I thought I played well in the final. It’s been a massive journey with so many ups and downs. I think it’s been well documented that I think I’ve underachieved in my career but you’ve got to enjoy this moment.

“It was a strong field this week and I felt like I played the best snooker and deserved to win the tournament. Jimmy White texted me this morning and so did Ken Doherty – we are all great friends and players get behind each other. Only one person can win and this was my week.”

![Image 15: Mark Allen kisses the trophy during the 2023 Snooker Champion of Champions in Bolton, England](https://seniorssnooker.com/wp-content/uploads/NZ9_0362-300x200.jpg)

Ward Wins Maiden Seniors Title
==============================

15th December 2025

[Home](https://wpbsa.com/) » Ward Wins Maiden Seniors Title

**Daniel Ward defeated Gerard Greene 4-2 to win the fifth World Seniors Tour event of the season the The Crucible Club in Reading.**

*   [Results](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/world-seniors-tour-event-5/results)

The victory marked a maiden win on the World Seniors Tour for the 44-year-old, who denied Greene a hat-trick of titles with victory in the title match in Berkshire.

![Image 7: Man in a black shirt, holding a trophy in front of a World Seniors backdrop](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/Ward-e1765801715818-300x242.jpg)

Five nations were represented at the event which was the fifth of nine in the series that offers qualification for next year’s World Seniors Snooker Championship at the Crucible Theatre.

Ward, who had reached the final of event two before losing out to Dharminder Lilly, survived an early scare by coming from 2-0 down against Neil Craycraft to advance as a 4-3 victor with breaks of 98, 83 and 61.

A 4-2 win against Stuart Watson followed to secure a place in the final day where he first met former World Seniors champion Aaron Canavan from Jersey.

The contest was closely contested as Ward led 2-0 and 3-1 but was forced into another deciding frame by his opponent.

![Image 8: Two middle-aged men, with cropped hair, are shaking hands in front of a backdrop with the words World Seniors printed on it](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/GreeneWard-300x230.jpg)

Ward was again able to come through the final frame by a 75-39 scoreline and then downed Philip Williams 4-2 to reach his second title match of the campaign.

There he faced former professional Greene, who was on an incredible run of 15 consecutive victories on the World Seniors Tour and aiming for a third successive title.

The first four frames of the final were shared, but it was Ward who pulled away with a break 52 in the fifth before getting over the line a 4-2 victor to earn his first title on the World Seniors Tour.

Hunter Victorious in Super Seniors
----------------------------------

![Image 9: A middle-aged man in a black shirt holds a trophy in front of a World Seniors backdrop](https://wpbsa.com/wp-content/uploads/HunterSS-300x288.jpg)

**John Hunter beat Neil Carroll 2-0 at The Crucible Club in Reading to win his second Super Seniors title of the season.**

*   [Results](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/super-seniors-event-5/results)

Nineteen players contested the Sunday event, which is open to all players aged over 55, and Hunter defeated both Wayne Martin and Simon Dent by a 2-0 scoreline to reach the final.

Carroll awaited him in the title match after earning victories over Raymond Grall, Dennis Tristram and Colin Bark.

It was the 59-year-old Hunter who came out on top in the final, completing another 2-0 win to secure the title without dropping a frame across the day.

**Event six of the World Seniors Tour takes place on 16-18 January 2026 at The Crucible Club in Reading. Enter now via [WPBSA SnookerScores](https://snookerscores.net/tournament-manager/world-seniors-tour-event-6).**
